verified: no two actions can target the same item
tables must be in the same AWS account and Region
aggregate item size cannot exceed 4 MB
all actions complete atomically or all fail
ClientRequestToken gives idempotency for 10 minutes after the first request completes; after 10 minutes the same token is treated as a new request
transaction ACID guarantees are Region-scoped and global replicas can transiently observe partial replication
TTL deletion is asynchronous and can take over 48 hours
AWS explicitly says not to rely on TTL deletes for lock records or state management when stale data must be removed in less than 48 hours

primary_source_verification.source: CockroachDB transaction-record / intent architecture and Parallel Commits
verified: transaction records and per-key write intents separate provisional writes from commit visibility
Parallel Commits introduces STAGING and permits implicit commit only when every listed write is proven successful
recovery consults listed writes and resolves to COMMITTED or ABORTED
primary_source_verification.scope_correction: The 2015 distributed-transactions blog explicitly warns that it describes a pre-beta design and points readers to newer architecture material. It remains a historical architectural precedent, not current drop-in application protocol evidence.

material_model_scope_defect.name: alias_factor_is_enumerated_but_unused_by_all_protocol_functions
material_model_scope_defect.evidence: The script includes alias in every scenario but atomic_txn, per_shard, intent_shards, staged_integrator and naive_partial never read s['alias']. Only targeted-slice predicates filter alias. Therefore the full-lattice results cannot be evidence that duplicate-item/alias inputs are canonicalized, rejected, or fail-closed.
material_model_scope_defect.consequence: Because alias is balanced and semantically ignored, every full-lattice protocol count is duplicated across alias=false/true. In particular, 108 of the 216 atomic safe terminals are alias=true by symmetry, yet DynamoDB forbids two actions on the same item. Those alias=true terminals are valid only under an external preprocessing assumption that the executable does not implement or test.
material_model_scope_defect.claim_status_change: The checkpoint's qualitative rule that same-item canonicalization is required is source-supported by AWS, but the finite model does NOT test that rule. Treat canonicalization/fail-closed-on-alias as NOT_DIRECTLY_TESTED by this artifact.

deadlock_microtest.code_observation: The arbitrary-order 36-pair count is computed. The result field canonical_global_order_deadlock_count is literal 0 rather than produced by a second simulation loop.
deadlock_microtest.independent_recomputation: Using the same simulate_orders semantics with both workers on canonical order (s1,s2,s3) yields both_done, not deadlock; thus the qualitative zero-deadlock canonical-order claim is independently reproduced for this toy scheduler despite not being mechanically generated in the worker result.
